issue_context.title: TiDB doesn't log any slow log if log.level >= "error"
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

1. Deploy a nightly cluster with config below:
```toml
[log]
level = "error"
slow-threshold = 0
```
2. Execute any query.
3. See whether there is the `tidb_slow_query.log` file.

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

slow logs show.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

No slow logs.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

[v5.1-v5.3], nightly
comments:
Introduced by https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/23534 which uses the same config of the server logger to initialize the slow query logger:
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/23534/files#diff-800042943fbf571b5e1b46f93f2ebab487a70873fd3c9708b00b39b9d59ce278R20.

The slow query logger uses default config before https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/23534/files#diff-163bbfde1f383898e507b5ca82bd6bec58809a82f6b8352d991f50962f7f472aL277-L285 and it uses `Debug` or `Warn` to log:
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/e97e8c0f238387c33cccca23f2434389f5f39c10/executor/adapter.go#L1028-L1031

We can use the default value of level to init the slow query logger here: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/dfd715763763805c01b79fa1ed8ec1c9492d04fd/util/logutil/slow_query_logger.go#L34

Slow query logger can always use `Warn()` to log slow query because it determines whether to log by execution duration, not by log level: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/dfd715763763805c01b79fa1ed8ec1c9492d04fd/executor/adapter.go#L1028-L1031
If so, we can add a test case here to check the level of slow query logger is always less than warn level: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/dfd715763763805c01b79fa1ed8ec1c9492d04fd/util/logutil/log_test.go#L117

@TonsnakeLin
Please check whether the issue should be labeled with 'affects-x.y' or 'fixes-x.y.z', and then remove 'needs-more-info' label.

review_comments:
`LogConfig{}.Level` set slowlogger to `info` level implicitly. Since `executor/adapter.go` logs slowlog with `warn()` method, this implicit setting could hide necessary information from developers.
IMHO it's better to explicitly set to `info` level.
```suggestion
	sqConfig.Level = zap.InfoLevel.String()
```

Yes, I fixed the bug just like you at begin. But I talked about it with @youjiali1995 and We two think that It‘s best not to expose zap.InfoLevel here.
Anyway, I think the two fixed methods all can work.

I would prefer to explicitly indicate that the default log level is INFO, and slow log will always use WARN to log so that it is always printed out.

Otherwise as a reader I will have no idea about how slow log will be outputted. What do you think? @youjiali1995

Using the default value indicates slow logger doesn't care about log level. I would like to delete the `Level` field of the config if I could. 

There is a test to cover the constraint that the default log level is less than warn level.
